sections.label: Major Wars
sections.description: Full-scale conventional conflicts that shaped India's modern military identity.

operations.name: Indo-Pakistani War (1947–48)
operations.objective: Defend Jammu & Kashmir following its accession to India and repel invading forces.
operations.result: Ceasefire — India retained Jammu, Kashmir Valley and Ladakh.
operations.description: The first war between India and Pakistan began after tribal forces backed by Pakistan invaded Jammu and Kashmir. Following the Instrument of Accession, Indian forces were airlifted to Srinagar and successfully prevented the capture of the Kashmir Valley.
operations.significance: Established the Line of Control's predecessor and secured Jammu, the Kashmir Valley and Ladakh under Indian administration.

operations.name: Sino-Indian War (1962)
operations.location: Ladakh and North-East Frontier Agency (present-day Arunachal Pradesh)
operations.objective: Defend India's northern borders against Chinese military offensives.
operations.result: Chinese unilateral ceasefire; China retained Aksai Chin.
operations.description: China launched coordinated attacks across both western and eastern sectors of the disputed border. Following intense fighting, China declared a unilateral ceasefire and withdrew in the eastern sector while retaining control over Aksai Chin.
operations.significance: Prompted major reforms and modernization of the Indian Armed Forces, transforming how India approached border security.

operations.name: Indo-Pakistani War (1965)
operations.objective: Repel Pakistani aggression launched through Operation Gibraltar and defend Indian territory.
operations.result: UN-mediated ceasefire; no territorial changes.
operations.description: The conflict began after Pakistan launched Operation Gibraltar in Jammu & Kashmir. India responded by opening multiple fronts across the international border, including a thrust towards Lahore, leading to one of the largest tank battles since World War II at the Battle of Asal Uttar.
operations.significance: Demonstrated India's ability to counter large-scale conventional attacks and strengthened future military modernization efforts.

operations.name: Indo-Pakistani War (1971)
operations.objective: Defend India against Pakistani air strikes and support the liberation of Bangladesh.
operations.result: Decisive Indian Victory — creation of Bangladesh.
operations.description: The war began after Pakistan launched pre-emptive air strikes on Indian airfields. Indian Armed Forces conducted coordinated operations on both fronts that led to the surrender of over 93,000 Pakistani troops and the creation of Bangladesh.
operations.significance: One of India's greatest military victories, resulting in the birth of Bangladesh and a major geopolitical shift in South Asia.

operations.name: Kargil War (1999)
operations.location: Kargil, Dras, Batalik and Mushkoh sectors, Ladakh
operations.objective: Evict Pakistani intruders occupying strategic heights along the Line of Control.
operations.result: Indian Victory — all major occupied positions regained.
operations.description: After Pakistani forces covertly occupied strategic heights along the Line of Control, India launched coordinated military operations — Operation Vijay on land and Operation Safed Sagar from the air — to recapture the positions. 26 July is observed as Kargil Vijay Diwas.
operations.significance: Reaffirmed the sanctity of the Line of Control and demonstrated India's capability to conduct high-altitude warfare under extreme conditions.

sections.label: Military Operations
sections.description: Named operations spanning integration of territories, overseas deployments, and precision strikes.

operations.name: Operation Polo
operations.objective: Integrate the princely State of Hyderabad into the Indian Union.
operations.result: Indian Victory — surrender of Nizam's forces within five days.
operations.description: Officially termed a 'Police Action', Operation Polo resulted in the rapid surrender of the Nizam's forces, leading to Hyderabad's accession to India.
operations.significance: Completed the political integration of one of India's largest and most strategically located princely states.

operations.name: Operation Bison
operations.location: Zoji La, Dras and Kargil, Ladakh
operations.objective: Recapture Zoji La Pass and reopen the land route to Ladakh.
operations.result: Indian Victory — Zoji La and Dras recaptured.
operations.description: Indian forces launched a surprise armoured assault through Zoji La using M5 Stuart tanks, recapturing the pass, Dras and eventually linking up with forces advancing from Leh.
operations.significance: Marked the world's highest-altitude use of tanks in combat at the time and secured Ladakh for India.

operations.name: Operation Vijay (Goa)
operations.objective: Liberate Goa, Daman and Diu from Portuguese colonial rule and integrate them into India.
operations.result: Indian Victory — Portuguese surrender within 36 hours.
operations.description: The Indian Armed Forces launched a coordinated land, air and naval campaign that resulted in the swift surrender of Portuguese forces, ending over 450 years of colonial rule.
operations.significance: Completed the territorial integration of Goa, Daman and Diu into India.

operations.name: Operation Meghdoot
operations.objective: Secure the Saltoro Ridge and Siachen Glacier before Pakistan could occupy the area.
operations.result: Indian Victory — dominant heights secured.
operations.description: A pre-emptive operation launched by the Indian Army and Indian Air Force to occupy the strategic heights of the Saltoro Ridge and Siachen Glacier. India secured the dominant positions, establishing control over the world's highest battlefield.
operations.significance: Established Indian control over the Siachen Glacier and denied Pakistan control of the strategically vital Saltoro Ridge.

operations.name: Operation Falcon
operations.objective: Counter Chinese military presence in the Sumdorong Chu Valley and secure Indian positions.
operations.result: Strategic success — escalation prevented.
operations.description: The Indian Army rapidly deployed troops to dominate the surrounding heights after Chinese incursions near Sumdorong Chu, preventing further escalation along the eastern sector.
operations.significance: Marked India's firm military response to Chinese border assertiveness and significantly improved India's posture along the eastern LAC.

operations.name: Operation Pawan
operations.objective: Disarm the LTTE and implement the Indo-Sri Lanka Accord as part of the IPKF mission.
operations.result: Mission completed — IPKF withdrew March 1990.
operations.description: Indian forces conducted large-scale combat operations against the LTTE after peace negotiations collapsed, carrying out conventional and counter-insurgency operations across northern Sri Lanka, including the Battle of Jaffna.
operations.significance: One of the Indian Army's largest overseas military operations and a defining experience in urban and jungle warfare tactics.

operations.name: Operation Cactus
operations.objective: Restore the legitimate government of the Maldives following an attempted coup.
operations.result: Indian Victory — government restored within hours.
operations.description: The Indian Armed Forces rapidly deployed paratroopers and a naval task force to Malé after a mercenary-backed coup attempt, securing the capital and restoring the elected government in under 24 hours.
operations.significance: Demonstrated India's rapid power projection capability and reinforced its role as the primary security guarantor in the Indian Ocean Region.

operations.name: Operation Vijay
operations.objective: Recapture Indian territory occupied by Pakistani forces during the Kargil conflict.
operations.result: Indian Victory — all major positions recaptured.
operations.description: Operation Vijay was the Indian Army's campaign during the Kargil War. Through sustained infantry assaults on near-vertical cliffs supported by artillery and air power, Indian forces regained all major occupied positions including Tololing, Tiger Hill and Point 4875.
operations.significance: Demonstrated exceptional courage and endurance at extreme altitude, and validated the importance of combined-arms warfare.

operations.name: Operation Safed Sagar
operations.objective: Provide air support to Indian Army ground operations during the Kargil War.
operations.result: Indian Victory — air superiority maintained.
operations.description: The Indian Air Force launched Operation Safed Sagar to support ground operations by striking enemy positions, supply routes and logistics under strict rules of engagement that prohibited crossing the Line of Control.
operations.significance: Marked the first large-scale combat use of air power by the IAF since 1971 and highlighted the importance of joint tri-service operations.

operations.name: Operation Ginger
operations.objective: Conduct a retaliatory cross-LoC raid following attacks on Indian soldiers.
operations.result: Operation Completed.
operations.description: Indian Army Special Forces carried out a covert cross-Line of Control raid targeting Pakistani military positions in retaliation for attacks on Indian troops along the LoC.
operations.significance: One of the earliest known modern cross-LoC retaliatory operations, foreshadowing the strategic shift formalised in 2016.

operations.name: Operation Hot Pursuit
operations.objective: Neutralize militant camps responsible for the Manipur ambush on Indian Army convoy.
operations.result: Indian Victory — militant camps destroyed.
operations.description: Following an ambush on an Indian Army convoy in Manipur that killed 18 soldiers, Indian Special Forces conducted a cross-border heliborne strike against insurgent camps along the Myanmar border.
operations.significance: Marked India's willingness to conduct precise cross-border counter-insurgency operations and signalled a shift in strategic posture.

operations.name: 2016 Surgical Strikes
operations.location: Line of Control, Pakistan-occupied Jammu & Kashmir
operations.objective: Destroy terrorist launch pads used for infiltration following the Uri attack.
operations.result: Indian Victory — multiple launch pads destroyed.
operations.description: The Indian Army conducted precision cross-Line of Control strikes on multiple terrorist launch pads in Pakistan-occupied Jammu & Kashmir following the Uri terrorist attack that killed 19 soldiers.
operations.significance: Established India's doctrine of publicly acknowledged precision cross-border retaliation against terrorist infrastructure.

operations.name: Operation Snow Leopard
operations.objective: Secure dominating heights along the LAC and strengthen India's defensive posture during the 2020 standoff.
operations.result: Strategic Success — Kailash Range heights secured.
operations.description: Indian Army formations including the Special Frontier Force occupied key heights on the Kailash Range south of Pangong Tso, gaining significant tactical advantage during the Eastern Ladakh standoff.
operations.significance: Provided India with a strong negotiating position during subsequent military and diplomatic talks with China, accelerating disengagement.

operations.name: Operation Sindoor
operations.objective: Destroy terrorist infrastructure linked to the Pahalgam terror attack.
operations.result: Operation Completed — multiple sites struck.
operations.description: India launched precision strikes against multiple terrorist infrastructure sites in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Jammu & Kashmir using missiles and loitering munitions, followed by a brief period of military escalation before a ceasefire understanding was reached.
operations.significance: Marked one of India's largest precision cross-border operations against terrorist infrastructure, demonstrating fully integrated tri-service capabilities.

sections.label: Internal Security Operations
sections.description: Operations to restore law and order within India's borders.

operations.name: Operation Blue Star
operations.objective: Remove heavily armed militants from the Golden Temple complex and restore law and order.
operations.result: Military objective achieved — militants removed.
operations.description: The Indian Army conducted Operation Blue Star to remove heavily armed militants who had fortified themselves inside the Golden Temple complex in Amritsar, following months of escalating violence in Punjab.
operations.significance: One of the most controversial internal security operations in independent India's history, with far-reaching political and social consequences.

sections.label: Counter-Insurgency Operations
sections.description: Long-running campaigns against insurgent groups in India's northeast and Jammu & Kashmir.

operations.name: Operation Rakshak
operations.objective: Counter insurgency, eliminate militant networks and maintain internal security in Jammu & Kashmir.
operations.result: Ongoing.
operations.description: Operation Rakshak is the Indian Army's long-running counter-insurgency campaign in Jammu & Kashmir, conducted alongside other security forces to combat terrorism and cross-border infiltration.
operations.significance: Represents one of the longest continuous counter-insurgency operations undertaken by the Indian Army, spanning over three decades.

operations.name: Operation Bajrang
operations.objective: Neutralize ULFA insurgents and dismantle militant infrastructure across Assam.
operations.result: Partial success — insurgent infrastructure weakened.
operations.description: The first large-scale counter-insurgency operation against ULFA, involving coordinated sweeps of militant camps, weapons caches and leadership hideouts across Upper Assam.
operations.significance: Marked the beginning of sustained military operations against insurgency in Assam and set the template for subsequent counter-ULFA campaigns.

operations.name: Operation Rhino
operations.objective: Continue counter-insurgency operations against ULFA and restore normalcy in Assam.
operations.result: Ongoing — ULFA significantly weakened.
operations.description: Launched after Operation Bajrang, Operation Rhino combined military operations with intelligence-based actions to dismantle ULFA's operational capabilities and infrastructure across the Brahmaputra valley.
operations.significance: Remains one of the Indian Army's longest-running counter-insurgency operations in Northeast India.

operations.name: Operation Sarp Vinash
operations.location: Hilkaka Forest, Poonch District, Jammu & Kashmir
operations.objective: Destroy militant bases and eliminate terrorist infiltration routes in the Hilkaka region.
operations.result: Indian Victory — largest militant stronghold dismantled.
operations.description: A month-long cordon-and-search operation conducted in the dense forests of Poonch that dismantled one of the largest militant strongholds in Jammu & Kashmir, involving over 6,000 troops.
operations.significance: Significantly weakened terrorist infrastructure in the Pir Panjal region and disrupted infiltration routes used to funnel militants from Pakistan.

operations.name: Operation All Out
operations.objective: Neutralize active terrorist networks through coordinated intelligence-based operations.
operations.result: Ongoing — significant leadership elimination achieved.
operations.description: A coordinated counter-terrorism campaign involving the Indian Army, Jammu & Kashmir Police and Central Armed Police Forces to eliminate terrorist leadership and infrastructure through intelligence-driven targeted operations.
operations.significance: Marked a decisive shift towards intelligence-driven, joint-force counter-terrorism in J&K, leading to a significant drop in active militant strength.

sections.label: Border Conflicts & Standoffs
sections.description: Military confrontations and standoffs along India's disputed borders.

operations.name: Operation Brasstacks
operations.objective: Conduct large-scale mechanised warfare exercises to validate operational doctrines.
operations.result: Exercise completed — triggered a near-crisis with Pakistan.
operations.description: One of the largest military exercises ever conducted by the Indian Army, involving massive troop and armour mobilisation in Rajasthan. Pakistan's counter-mobilisation on its borders brought the two countries close to armed confrontation.
operations.significance: Demonstrated India's large-scale conventional warfare capability and had significant strategic implications for South Asian military planning.

operations.name: Galwan Valley Clash
operations.objective: Defend Indian positions and enforce disengagement agreements along the Line of Actual Control.
operations.result: Indian positions held — casualties on both sides.
operations.description: Indian and Chinese troops engaged in violent hand-to-hand combat in the Galwan Valley, resulting in the deaths of 20 Indian soldiers (including Colonel Santosh Babu) and an unconfirmed number of Chinese casualties — the first fatalities on the India-China border in 45 years.
operations.significance: Fundamentally altered India's military and diplomatic posture along the Line of Actual Control and accelerated defence modernization and infrastructure development.

operations.name: Yangtse Clash
operations.objective: Prevent Chinese troops from altering the status quo along the Line of Actual Control.
operations.result: Indian positions held — Chinese attempt repelled.
operations.description: Approximately 300 Chinese troops attempted to unilaterally change the status quo at Yangtse in the Tawang sector. Indian troops successfully resisted the incursion in a face-off that involved hand-to-hand contact, resulting in minor injuries on both sides.
operations.significance: Reaffirmed India's resolve and capability to defend the eastern sector of the LAC and prompted further reinforcement of the Arunachal border.
